title: feat(plugin-auth)!: an SSO provider is edited in place, its delete names who it unlinks and removes its mappings and grants, one domain has one provider
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBLcR66HDKGmkegYSEN3PSwY)_

Fixes #32085

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/**` teaches no SSO provider registration, domain claim, edit or delete (no hit for `sso/register`, `delete-provider`, `register_sso_provider` or an SSO provider domain in `skills/`)

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:SSO 提供方可以原地编辑(SAML 证书轮换、SSO URL、实体 ID;OIDC client id/secret、scopes),删除前后都说清会解绑多少用户、其中多少人没有关联其他登录方式(没有密码,也没有其他提供方),删除后清掉该提供方的组映射和它投影出的授权;同一邮箱域名不能再注册第二个提供方。
- 为什么改:之前轮换 IdP 证书只能删了重建,而删除会静默解绑所有 SSO 用户;两个提供方抢同一域名时,第二个不会按地址被路由到。
- 风险与回滚:属于收窄(BREAKING):以前能注册成功的“同一域名第二个提供方”现在被拒(它以前存上了也不会按地址被路由到),拒绝信息给出补救:用它自己的域名条目(子域名仍可)、把该域名从现有提供方上改掉,或先删除现有提供方;读不到提供方表时,注册和改域名回 503;删除时读不到受影响人数也回 503。已存的提供方不受影响。回滚即回退本 PR。删除仍然允许(席位裁定),只是说清后果。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`,再看 `register-sso-provider.ts` 末尾的编辑桥。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts src/admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts`。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**Seat ruling recorded (server seat 2, on the card's two-way Expected for delete):** the second option. Delete stays possible, because an administrator decommissioning an identity provider must be able to; its confirmation and its answer name how many linked users it unlinks and how many of them have no other sign-in method linked (no password, no other provider). Same-id re-registration restoring links is not owed: with the edit door in place, certificate rotation no longer goes through delete.

### 1. The edit door

- `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/update-provider` (platform-admin gated, ADR-0068 D4, like every `/admin/sso/*` bridge), served by two new `sys_sso_provider` actions:
  - **Edit SAML Settings**: `issuer` (IdP entity ID, filled from the row), `entryPoint` (IdP SSO URL), `cert` (new signing certificate, checked as X.509), `keepCurrentCert` (trust the stored certificate beside the new one while the IdP switches over; a later edit without it drops the old one).
  - **Edit OIDC Settings**: `clientId`, `clientSecret` (`password`, write-only, never read back into the form), `scopes`.
- Measured on `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12: `/sso/update-provider` merges member by member (`mergeSAMLConfig` / `mergeOIDCConfig`, `updates.X ?? current.X`) and replaces only `mapping` whole. So the bridge sends only the members that changed and never `mapping`: a blank field keeps what is stored, and the stored attribute mapping (with its `extraFields`) stands through every edit.
- The vendor treats the SAML entity ID and SSO URL and the OIDC client ID as the provider's identity and refuses changing them while an account is linked (`409`); the bridge relays that refusal and says why. A certificate or client secret is not identity and changes with users linked.
- Not offered: the OIDC issuer. The vendor resolves an OIDC provider's endpoints from discovery at registration only and an update keeps them, so a new issuer would be saved while sign-in kept going to the old IdP; the bridge refuses it `400` and says to register a new provider.
- The stored configuration (an `internal` field the form cannot read) says which protocol a provider speaks, so both actions are offered on every row and a field of the other protocol is refused `400` naming the right action.
- The answer names the changed fields, never a value.

### 2. Delete consequences and cleanup

- **Before:** the delete action's `preflight` reads `GET /api/v1/auth/admin/sso/delete-impact?providerId=` (platform-admin gated, closed query set): users unlinked, users with no other sign-in method linked (no password, no other provider), group mappings and projected grants, plus one sentence naming them. The action's confirmation text says the same in words.
- **On the door itself:** the existing `/sso/delete-provider` before-hook (after the #30300 sign-in method floor) counts the same before the vendor writes, so every caller of the vendor route is counted, not only the console. A count that cannot be read refuses the delete `503`, because an unlink cannot be taken back.
- **After a delete the vendor answered `success`:** the after-hook removes the provider's `sys_idp_group_mapping` rows (`source_kind: 'sso'`, `source_id` = provider id) and the `sys_user_permission_set` grants whose `reason` is exactly `sso-group-projection: provider '<id>'` (never by permission-set name), through the data engine, then adds `data` to the answer: `unlinkedUsers`, `usersWithoutOtherSignIn`, `removedGroupMappings`, `removedGrants`, `dependentsRemoved`, `message`. A grant by hand, another provider's grant, another provider's mapping and SCIM mappings are untouched. A refused delete (`403`, `404`) runs no cleanup and carries no counts. A cleanup that fails is said in the answer (`dependentsRemoved: false`) and once at `error` with the remedy.
- `scim-group-projection.ts` and `sys-idp-group-mapping.object.ts` are untouched (#32121 owns them); the marker comes from the exported `ssoGroupProjectionReason`.
- The two cleanup deletes are new tenant-audit census sites: typed receiver, literal options, each grant deleted with its own organization as the tenant. `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` are regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, and the page's hand-written figures follow (two more write call sites).

### 3. One email domain, one provider

- `/sso/register` (both the direct door and the `/admin/sso/register` / `register-saml` bridges) and a domain edit on `/sso/update-provider` onto a domain another provider already serves are refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with `field: 'domain'`, before the vendor writes. The holder is named (`heldBy` and in the message) to a platform administrator; any other caller (an organization administrator editing their own provider) is told only that the domain is served. The message says why (sign-in routes an address to one provider by its domain, so a second provider for it would not be reached by address) and what to do instead: register it under its own domain entry (a subdomain stays accepted), edit the domain off the provider that serves it, or delete that provider first. A provider-table read that fails refuses the register or domain edit `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and nothing is saved.
- **Refuse, not warn; measured:** the vendor routes an address to the provider whose `domain` equals it exactly, else the first whose comma-separated list matches it (subdomains included), so a second provider on the same entry would not be reached by address. The one legitimate two-provider shape is a subdomain beside its parent (`eng.acme.com` beside `acme.com`: exact match wins for the subdomain), so only an exact entry collides and that shape is accepted, both ways round. Entries are compared as bare lower-case hosts (`https://ACME.com/` is `acme.com`).
- The register bridges now relay the located refusal (`code`, `field`, `heldBy`) as it came; every other refusal keeps their own code as before.
- **This is the `(narrowing)` arm:** such a register or domain edit succeeded before (the second provider was saved, and would not be reached by address), and the `503`s above (a register or domain edit when the providers cannot be read, a delete when its count cannot be read) are new refusals too. Providers already stored are not re-checked; the changeset carries the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition (`no-migration-prescription`).

### Console

What the console still owes beyond these declared actions (a provider edit form beyond declared actions, the group-mapping add/remove form, and drawing the delete preflight for a caller the platform-admin read refuses) is #32185.

## Tests

- `src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts` (new, 18 cases): real ObjectQL over better-sqlite3, real `AuthManager` with the real `sso()` plugin, real sign-ups and cookies, real `AuthPlugin` route registration. Covers the preflight (counts, sentence, `404`, closed query `400`), the delete answer and cleanup (mappings and marker grants only), refused delete, unreadable count `503`, failed cleanup; domain collision on direct register (four spellings incl. a multi-domain list; the message carries the by-address reason and the remedy), via the SAML bridge, on update-provider, self re-save allowed, non-admin not told the holder, subdomain controls both ways; SAML cert rotation with a linked user, `keepCurrentCert` overlap then drop, SSO URL refused while linked, entity ID and SSO URL changed while unlinked, bad cert / wrong-protocol / empty edit `400`; OIDC secret replaced while linked and never answered, scopes replaced, client ID refused while linked; the action declarations.
- `src/admin-sso-bridge-gate.test.ts`: both new doors answer anonymous `401`, member / org admin / position-named `403` without reading or writing the provider, platform admin admitted.
- `src/auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts`: both routes added to the objectstack-sourced pin; ledger rows in `auth-route-ledger.ts`.
- `packages/platform-objects/src/platform-objects.test.ts`: the credential roster names the new `password` param (`edit_oidc_provider.clientSecret`).
- Translations: the new strings are regenerated with `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write` and translated in all ten locale bundles.

### Ablations (committed first, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to HEAD)

| # | Mutation (file) | Test that went red |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | after-hook settle call → `void 0` (`auth-manager-after-hook.ts`) | the delete answers the counts, and removes the provider mappings and the grants carrying its marker only |
| A2 | register domain check removed (`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`) | direct /sso/register onto a served domain … |
| A3 | update-provider domain check removed (`auth-manager-before-hook.ts`) | a domain edit onto a served domain … |
| A4 | exact-entry match → always collide (`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`) | a subdomain beside its parent … (control) |
| A5 | holder named to every caller (`auth-manager.ts`) | … not a platform administrator … |
| A6 | `keepCurrentCert` ignored (`register-sso-provider.ts`) | keepCurrentCert … |
| A7 | unreadable count → let the delete through (`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`) | a count that cannot be read … |
| A8 | grant query by organization instead of the exact marker (`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`) | the delete answers the counts … marker only |
| A9 | closed query check removed (`register-sso-provider.ts`) | the preflight read refuses … |
| A10 | admin gate removed from the edit door (`auth-plugin.ts`) | 4 of 5 `POST /admin/sso/update-provider` gate cases (anonymous, member, org admin, position-named) |
| A11 | edit answer echoes the update (`register-sso-provider.ts`) | the client secret is replaced … |
| A12 | mapping delete skipped (`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`) | the delete answers the counts … |
| A13 | marker grant delete skipped (`sso-provider-lifecycle.ts`) | the delete answers the counts … |
| A14 | SAML edit sends a `mapping` (`register-sso-provider.ts`) | a SAML signing certificate rotates … (stored mapping lost its `extraFields`) |
| A15 | OIDC edit sends a `mapping` (`register-sso-provider.ts`) | an OIDC client secret is replaced … (stored mapping lost its `extraFields`) |

Each mutation landed (anchor 1 → 0, blob changed), the named test failed, and the file was restored to HEAD (`git diff HEAD` empty). A1, A12 and A13 were run again at `6bf414ee`, after the cleanup writes were retyped for the tenant audit census and `origin/main` was merged; A14 and A15 ran at `9dad77ea`.

## Verification

The delete preview label, confirmation and answer name the count as users with no other sign-in method linked (no password, no other provider); the count and who may read it are unchanged. The changeset's refusal list names the `503` a register or domain edit gets when the SSO providers cannot be read.
